target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
2025 D031 is a composite disclosure covering three specific aspects of the Mainframe portfolio: Cybersecurity & Compliance Management, Beyond Code Programs, and Foundational Solutions. 2024 D052 (Identity & Access Management/Cybersecurity), D053 (Compliance & Data Protection), and D047 (Beyond Code Programs) map directly to the specific components detailed in D031. D031 explicitly describes managing mainframe access (D052), compliance/protecting data (D053), and Beyond Code programs (D047). This is a valid many-to-one link.

2024 disclosure D054 describes the Security Insights Platform for mainframe security posture. 2025 disclosure D031 describes Cybersecurity & Compliance Management, which explicitly mentions protecting crucial mainframe data, identifying risk, and supporting external security managers, aligning with the mainframe security subject. While the naming changed, the specific subject of mainframe security management is preserved.

previous_disclosures.summary: Beyond Code programs address skills development, staffing, change management, and cost-saving initiatives to help customers maximize mainframe investments and drive business success.
Identity & Access Management solutions manage mainframe access with modern practices like multi-factor authentication and privileged user management, supporting external security managers.
These solutions protect crucial mainframe data to ensure compliance, identify risk, and reduce security management load through automated identification and authorization cleanup.

The Security Insights Platform helps ensure a trusted environment by interpreting mainframe security posture, identifying risks, and developing remediation steps, with data available for in-house security tools.

current_disclosures.summary: Cybersecurity & Compliance Management aligns mainframe platforms with enterprise security mandates and protects crucial data; Beyond Code Programs upskill workforces and improve efficiency; Foundational & Open Mainframe Solutions deliver mission-critical core capabilities and modern, API-driven cloud-integrated tools.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company promotes from within for leadership roles and offers manager/leadership development programs, specialized training, and tuition reimbursement for eligible employees.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose specific programs aimed at employee skills development and career advancement. AVGO's 'Beyond Code Programs' focus on skills development and upskilling within the context of mainframe technology to help customers, while AMD offers specialized manager/leadership development programs and tuition reimbursement to help its own employees advance their careers. While AVGO's initiative is framed as a customer value-add service, AMD's is an internal human capital investment; however, both explicitly address 'skills development' and 'training' as key mechanisms for workforce capability. AVGO states its programs address 'skills development, staffing... and educating and upskilling the workforce' (avgo_2024_1_P025_S012), whereas AMD states it 'provide[s] specialized development programs for our employees as well as educational assistance in the form of tuition reimbursement' (amd_2024_1_P085_S003).

sentences.text: • Beyond Code Programs: These value-added offerings help ensure our customers get the most out of their mainframe investments. These offerings unlock additional value for organizations in areas such as educating and upskilling the workforce, providing expert guidance and support for change events, and uncovering opportunities to improve efficiency and save costs.

Our manager and leadership development programs are highly rated, and we provide specialized development programs for our employees as well as educational assistance in the form of tuition reimbursement for eligible employees to continue their university education or achieve advanced certifications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Talent Development and Employee Engagement Initiatives
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel invests in talent development through training programs, rotational assignments, updated job architecture, mentoring, and employee resource groups. Employee perceptions are gathered via annual surveys, and a portion of executive and employee performance bonuses is linked to improvements in employee experience survey results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Intel disclose investments in talent development programs focused on building employee skills. AVGO's Beyond Code programs are described as helping ensure customers get the most out of investments through 'educating and upskilling the workforce' (avgo_2024_1_P025_S012). Similarly, Intel invests in talent development through 'training programs' and helps employees 'build skills' via updated job architecture and custom learning curricula (intc_2024_1_P057_S001, intc_2024_1_P057_S002). Both disclosures highlight structured learning and upskilling as a core component of their talent strategy.

comparisons.comparison: While AVGO focuses on customer-facing upskilling and staff support through Beyond Code, Micron focuses on internal compensation equity and benefits design to support employee well-being. AVGO's disclosure emphasizes 'cost-saving initiatives' and 'expert guidance' for customers (avgo_2024_1_P025_S004), whereas Micron's disclosure highlights that its compensation programs are designed to support 'team members' financial and personal wellbeing' through total compensation strategy (mu_2024_1_P075_S001, mu_2024_1_P075_S002). Both disclosures relate to the broader 'Human Capital & Organization' taxonomy and the strategic use of financial and developmental resources, but AVGO's is external/customer-centric while Micron's is internal/compensation-centric.

Both companies view structured education and skill-building as critical, with AVGO applying it to customer mainframe success and NVIDIA applying it to internal career advancement and readiness.
